env.name: ASPNETCORE_URLS
env.why: The address Kestrel binds. src/Readings/Program.cs calls WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args) and there is no Properties/launchSettings.json, so without this the host falls back to its built-in default (:5000) and nothing would be listening where app_url points. This is the app's own real origin inside the sandbox, not a placeholder.

env.name: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT
env.why: Selects the host environment. Development keeps the developer exception page and per-request logging on, so a verifier reading the run log sees which endpoint failed and why instead of a bare 500. No code branches on it; the host does.

env.name: DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT
env.why: The .NET SDK's first run posts usage telemetry. The sandbox should not make a network call the repo never asked for.

env.name: DOTNET_NOLOGO
env.why: Suppresses the SDK first-run banner so the tail of a failing build is the failure rather than the welcome message.

env.name: VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_DIRECTORY
env.why: Added by the amendment. VSTest 18.12.0 (the version in SDK 11) prints 'VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_DIRECTORY environment variable was not found, falling back to a user-private temporary directory. This is most likely caused by an outdated Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk package reference' on every run here, because the test project pins Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 17.12.0. The warning is the last line of test output and it sent the builder looking at the package version rather than at its own container. Naming the directory removes the fallback and the warning; the test command creates it first, because VSTest does not. Toolchain configuration, in the same class as DOTNET_NOLOGO — nothing in src/ or tests/ reads it.

dropped.why: That step provisions an SDK on a bare runner; it is CI plumbing, not something the app needs installed. The trial runner already ships .NET SDKs, and a newer SDK builds this repo's net9.0 target fine — verified here against SDK 11.0.100, which produced 0 warnings with TreatWarningsAsErrors on.

dropped.what: dotnet test --no-build as the sandbox's test command
dropped.why: Replaced by the amendment, not dropped as a step: the tests still run, through `dotnet vstest` on the built assembly. The builder reported `dotnet test --no-build` exiting 0 while discovering and running nothing in its agent container — no console output, no trx, no --diag file. It works in both containers checked here (6 passed), so the difference is in the role container and not visible from either of them. The shape of that failure is what matters: a gate that reads only an exit code reports green over zero tests. `dotnet vstest` skips `dotnet test`'s project evaluation entirely and is the one form the builder confirmed working there, and the command asserts a positive result count on top. CI keeps running `dotnet test`; it is checked on a GitHub runner, where it works.

It is a lint gate, not a build or a test. `bsf gates static` runs the repo's own linters, and folding it into `test` would make a whitespace nit report as a failing test. The runbook carries the form that works — `dotnet restore && dotnet format --verify-no-changes --no-restore` — and the bare form from CI is not it; see the amendment's episode for why.

dropped.what: The bare `dotnet build` / `dotnet test` forms, without --no-restore / --no-build
dropped.why: Kept the staged forms instead so install, build and test are three separable steps the trial can attribute a failure to; the README's forms re-restore and re-build on every invocation.

the six xUnit tests in tests/Readings.Tests/ReadingStoreTests.cs, covering every public member of ReadingStore (TryAdd, For, MeanCelsius), run against the built assembly

dotnet format --verify-no-changes against .editorconfig over both projects, including the style half over tests/Readings.Tests — proven by a scratch file with a block-scoped namespace raising IDE0161 and a scratch file with bad whitespace raising WHITESPACE, both then deleted
a browser screenshot of GET /sensors/boiler/readings after the run command seeds three readings, so a change to the JSON shape is visible and not only asserted

not_exercised.what: Whatever makes `dotnet test --no-build` silently find nothing in a role's agent container. The amendment routes around it; it did not reproduce it, so the cause is unknown and uncaught.
not_exercised.why: Both containers available here run `dotnet test --no-build` correctly (6 passed), including with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR set to a missing directory, with the test project's bin/ deleted, and with its obj/project.assets.json deleted. If the same condition reaches the sandbox, the test command still fails loudly rather than passing — but nothing here detects the condition itself, so a role that hits it sees a failing test gate and not an explanation.

not_exercised.what: Anything that survives a restart. ReadingStore is a ConcurrentDictionary in process memory and the repo has no database, file store or migration, so state in the sandbox lasts exactly as long as the run command.
not_exercised.why: There is nothing to persist to. A change that introduced a store needs an amendment adding that service to the sandbox; nothing here would catch a persistence bug.

not_exercised.what: Concurrent writes. TryAdd takes a lock on the per-sensor list and the dictionary is concurrent, but no test and no trial step issues two overlapping requests.
not_exercised.why: Every test constructs its own store on one thread and the trial drives the API one curl at a time. A race in the lock or sort would pass everything here.

not_exercised.what: The HTTP layer under the test command. Program.cs is declared `public partial class Program` specifically so a test project could host it, but tests/Readings.Tests references neither Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing nor WebApplicationFactory, so routing, model binding and JSON serialisation have no automated test.
not_exercised.why: The trial reaches these paths over real HTTP and the screenshot shows the serialised shape, but a regression in them fails no test, so the test gate alone will not catch it.

not_exercised.what: Coverage measurement. No coverage collector is configured in either csproj, and .factory/guardrails/coverage.json has high_pct and floor_pct at 0.
not_exercised.why: The test command emits no coverage data here, so the coverage half of gate 2 has nothing to read. Turning it on needs a collector package added to the test project.

not_exercised.what: A second test project. The test command names one assembly path explicitly.
not_exercised.why: `dotnet vstest` takes assembly paths, not a solution, so a new test project under tests/ runs nowhere until the test command names it too. That is a manifest amendment, and until it happens the new project's tests pass silently by not existing to the gate. The count guard does not help: the one named assembly still reports its own results.
None are configured anywhere in the repo. ASPNETCORE_URLS is http on loopback, so there is no TLS path and no identity to assert against.

episode.observed: Neither reproduced. `dotnet test --no-build` ran 6 tests and passed; `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` exited 0. Same SDK the builder named, 11.0.100, and the same VSTest 18.12.0. The only common ground with the report was the trailing warning: 'VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_DIRECTORY environment variable was not found, falling back to a user-private temporary directory. This is most likely caused by an outdated Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk package reference in the test project.'

episode.tried: Pushed the environment at the failure instead of guessing: ran `dotnet test --no-build` with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR set to the missing /run/user/1001, with TMPDIR set to a missing directory, with HOME set to a missing directory, and with tests/Readings.Tests/bin deleted.
episode.observed: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR made no difference (6 passed). TMPDIR missing crashed MSBuild with a stack trace, exit 82. HOME missing crashed the CLI's first-run configurer, exit 1. bin/ deleted gave 'The argument ...Readings.Tests.dll is invalid', exit 1. Every one of them fails loudly. episode.changed: Nothing. Ruled out the environment variables the sandbox could plausibly be getting wrong, which is what left 'route around it' as the answer for the test command rather than 'fix the cause'.

episode.tried: The format failure, which is the more tractable half. Moved tests/Readings.Tests/obj/project.assets.json aside — leaving bin/ intact — and ran `dotnet format --verify-no-changes --no-restore`.
episode.observed: Reproduced exactly: 'error CS0246: The type or namespace name FactAttribute could not be found', once per [Fact], exit 2. Restoring the file put it back to exit 0. The asymmetry in the builder's report is explained by the same thing: src/Readings has zero PackageReference entries, so it resolves with no assets at all, while tests/Readings.Tests cannot find xunit without them. `dotnet test --no-build` in the same broken state still ran all 6 tests — so bad restore state breaks format and not test, and the two failures the builder saw have different causes.
episode.changed: Made the lint command restore explicitly before formatting, and then forbid format's own implicit restore: `dotnet restore && dotnet format --verify-no-changes --no-restore`. The restore guarantees the assets the workspace load needs; --no-restore stops a second, differently-configured restore from running inside format, which is the only thing in that command that touches the network. Recorded in the runbook, which is where the lint command lives — the manifest schema has no field for it.
